subject: Switchover consistency & priority matrix — Redwood SLA question
messages:
From: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@ledgertech.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
Cc: procurement@ledgertech.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:13:00 -0400
Subject: Switchover consistency & priority matrix — Redwood SLA question

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our ops and risk teams reviewed Redwood's standard failover language and came back with a couple of specific asks that will affect acceptance for production. High level: LedgerTech needs tighter guarantees around regional switchover consistency (RPO bounds across geo replicas) and a clear priority matrix so we know which datasets/services get warm standby vs cold standby.

Specific items attached in the spreadsheet (LedgerTech-SLA-Risk-Spreadsheet.xlsx):
- Column A: dataset classification (P0/P1/P2) and required RPO in seconds/minutes
- Column B: target switchover sequence and who owns network DNS cutover
- Column C: requested liability carveouts for cross-border replication

Two concrete asks: 1) Can Redwood guarantee a 15-minute RTO for P0 routing within the primary+hot-standby pair in the US-east/US-west pair? 2) For P1 datasets, LedgerTech needs a written plan that describes data consistency model during the switchover (eventual vs applied-kv).

We know this is negotiable, so if you can propose a prioritized acceptance matrix plus any exception language we can escalate internally. We have procurement timelines for the quarter close, so a response by Friday 4/9 would be ideal.

Best,
Tom
Procurement Lead | LedgerTech

Attachment: LedgerTech-SLA-Risk-Spreadsheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)

From: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
To: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@ledgertech.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Switchover consistency & priority matrix — Redwood SLA question

Tom —

Appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Internal quick read: LedgerTech's classification and timeline are reasonable for a high-touch enterprise deal, but there are a few operational constraints we need to call out up front to align expectations. Below are our proposed responses and a request for two clarifying details so we can finalize a formal SOW addendum:

1) P0 RTO (15 minutes) within a primary/hot-standby pair (US-east / US-west):
- Our standard dedicated configuration can meet a 15-minute RTO for compute routing and KV-prefix warm-cache restoration if the customer maintains cross-region warm-standby and agrees to the warm-standby activation window (we recommend 0-30 minutes prep).
- Exception request: For multi-tenant hosted deployments we cannot guarantee strict 15 minutes without a Dedicated reservation and a documented activation runbook.

2) P1 data consistency during switchover:
- By default Redwood provides eventual consistency guarantees for async cross-region replication. For strong applied-consistency during switchover, we can offer an optional sync-safe replication mode for the P0 set (additional throughput/cost impact).

Clarifying items we need from your side:
- Which specific datasets (by name or dataset id) are P0 vs P1? (the spreadsheet helps, but we need canonical ids)
- Are you planning to use our Dedicated or Hosted offering for this environment? Dedicated is recommended for the 15-minute RTO ask.

Next steps: Jonas and Marissa are looping in infra to draft a negotiation matrix and an SOW addendum that maps P0/P1 -> activation owner, expected RTO/RPO, and liability carveouts. We can have a first draft over to you by EOD Thu 4/8 if we get the canonical dataset ids today.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
Phone: +1 415-555-1284

Attachment: none

From: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
To: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Switchover consistency & priority matrix — Redwood SLA question

Irene / Marissa —

Looping infra notes and a proposed internal carve we should present. Quick summary (see attached internal-failover-proposal.pdf):
- Accept 15-minute RTO for P0 within US-east/US-west if LedgerTech commits to Dedicated (reserved capacity) and explicit warm-cache retention TTL of 48h for target prefixes. This requires a small SLA surcharge (we should flag pricing).
- For P1, offer documented eventual consistency + a playbook that enumerates the manual stabilization steps (DNS TTL manipulation, routing cutover checklist, reconciliation window).
- Liability: propose a mutual-limited liability clause for cross-region data loss where the customer owns last-mile replication confirmation for P1 datasets; Redwood will accept responsibility for in-region compute failover for P0 only if activation follows the agreed runbook within the activation window.

We should attach the internal PDF (internal-failover-proposal.pdf) and then send a single consolidated SOW addendum + DocuSign link to LedgerTech. Draft language included in the PDF; I pulled a precedent from FinServe SOW for wording on activation owner and liability buckets.

Jonas
VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Attachment: internal-failover-proposal.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

Tom —

Thanks for the spreadsheet and for the clear priorities. Attached is a consolidated SOW addendum and the negotiated liability matrix we discussed (redwood-revised-sow-docusign.pdf). Highlights: 

- P0 (critical datasets): 15-minute RTO for compute routing within US-east/US-west when using Redwood Dedicated + 48h warm-cache retention. Activation owner: LedgerTech follows our runbook to trigger failover; Redwood will execute the compute cutover and KV-restore.
- P1 (important): documented eventual consistency; Redwood will provide a stabilization playbook and a 4-hour reconciliation window post-activation.
- Cross-region data loss carveout: mutual-limited liability for async replication; explicit exceptions listed per dataset id in Appendix A.
- Pricing note: a small monthly premium applies for guaranteed warm-cache retention and the sync-safe replication option for P0.

If this looks good I can send the DocuSign envelope for signatures. We expect the signed SOW addendum to become an addendum to your primary MSA and will push the Dedicated provisioning once counters are received.

Requested next step from you: confirm P0 dataset ids (matching Appendix A) and indicate whether you accept the Dedicated reservation recommendation. If yes, I'll send DocuSign today.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-revised-sow-docusign.pdf (PDF, 124KB)
